sentences.text: Ctenosauriscus was an extinct sail-backed archosaur that lived in what is now northern Germany.
Its most defining trait is a prominent sail on its back, created by neural spines on the vertebrae that could reach up to 12 times the height of the vertebral bodies.
This creature is considered one of the oldest known archosaurs, sharing this distinction with Vytshegdosuchus and Xilousuchus.
The holotype skeleton, which is the specimen the species is based on, was discovered in early 1871 near the locality of Bremke dell close to Göttingen, Germany.
Friedrich von Huene first described the species in 1902, initially naming it Ctenosaurus koeneni.
The genus name was later changed to Ctenosauriscus in 1964 by Oskar Kuhn because the original name was already taken by a lizard.
A major redescription of the holotype was published in 2011 by a team of six paleontologists.
A 1998 study hypothesized that Ctenosauriscus was bipedal and that its sail helped absorb forces from walking on two legs.
However, a 2011 study rejected this bipedal hypothesis, arguing that the spine's mechanics would require impossible muscle connections to the knee.
Xiphosurans, or horseshoe crabs, found in the same formation may have been prey for Ctenosauriscus.
The parent group of Ctenosauriscus is Ctenosauriscidae.
Ctenosauriscus is classified in the class Reptilia.
Ctenosauriscus lived during the latest Olenekian stage of the Early Triassic, approximately 247.5 to 247.2 million years ago.
It inhabited an arid floodplain environment with dry sabkha-like areas and wetter zones resembling modern swamps within the Solling Formation of Northern Germany.
